reconcile.connective: Defenders read Deuteronomy 7 as a targeted ban on the idolatrous Canaanite nations — admitting proselytes and falling outside Joseph's Egyptian marriage — not a blanket prohibition on all foreign unions.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells presses the objection at the source: God forbids intermarriage on pain of being "destroyed suddenly," yet Joseph married an Egyptian priest's daughter and Moses a foreign wife with no punishment — so the standard is applied inconsistently.

excerpts.excerpt_text: Unless they became proselytes, as Rahab, who was married by Salmon, and so those of other nations, as Ruth the Moabitess, and so any captive taken in war; otherwise it was not lawful, bad consequences have followed upon it, which it is the design of this law to prevent; that is, being snared and drawn aside into idolatry, which was the case of Solomon …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly distinguishes the senses: the ban is not absolute — it admits proselytes and captives, and its purpose is to prevent idolatry, not to condemn every foreign marriage like Joseph's. NOT shipped.

excerpts.excerpt_text: The strict prohibition against contracting any alliances with such infamous idolaters was a prudential rule, founded on the experience that "evil communications corrupt good manners" [Co1 15:33], and its importance or necessity was attested by the unhappy examples of Solomon and others in the subsequent history of Israel.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Frames the ban as a prudential rule aimed at idolaters specifically, not all foreigners — supports limiting Deut 7 to the Canaanite-idolatry danger and excluding cases like Joseph's. Distinct voice from Gill. NOT shipped.

pd_work.resource: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63), on Deuteronomy 7:3
pd_work.author: John Gill
pd_work.note: Gill treats this passage directly, limiting the intermarriage ban to non-proselyte idolaters and noting proselyte/captive exceptions (Rahab, Ruth) — the harmonizing answer to Joseph's Egyptian marriage. Used in place of Haley because his coverage of this specific pair could not be confirmed.
